root_idea.summary: The lexical analysis presents three root orientations: flashing or restless movement, sound or cry, and a cause or bond that is maintained and protected.
root_idea.development: For the noun إِلّ, the supported semantic development follows the maintained-bond orientation into kinship, covenant, sacred right, and reported theological readings. The flashing and acoustic material remains a root-level Classical orientation rather than a Quranic gloss for إِلّ.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is displayed under the normalized citation form إِلّ.

senses.definition: A tie of kinship or relationship; nearness in kindred.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction لا يرقبون في مؤمن إِلًّا, the term is interpreted as a relationship or kinship bond.

senses.definition: A compact, covenant, confederacy, or protective bond; an assurance of safety or security.
senses.usage_conditions: In the same Quranic construction, the term is also interpreted as a covenant or obligation of protection and security.
A reported interpretation of the Quranic term identifies it with lordship or divine governance.
A reported interpretation of the Quranic term identifies it with God; this interpretation is disputed in the cited lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The definite article, marking a noun as known or determinate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may identify something through prior mention, mental conception, or present contextual reference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The article in generic use, denoting a species, its individuals collectively, the totality of its characteristic properties, or its essence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The scope may be the whole class, the comprehensive properties represented in one exemplar, or the species as a quiddity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The article marking a noun's predominant or conventionally salient referent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Context supplies a referent treated as the leading or familiar instance of the noun, such as the culturally understood city or book.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The article prefixed to a transferred proper name to allude to the name's original lexical meaning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The prefix may be retained when the original descriptive sense is intended and omitted when only the proper name is intended.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relative element equivalent to الذي and its variants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is prefixed especially to active and passive participles; extension to epithets, adverbs, or propositions is reported as exceptional or chiefly poetic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An interrogative particle equivalent to هل, meaning whether or did.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a rare Classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything regarded as sacred or inviolable, or a right pertaining to such a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a broader Classical lexical use distinct from the specific Quranic interpretations listed above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A good or sound origin; a source or provenance free from defect, suspicion, or disrepute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe the origin of a person or thing, or the person or source from which it originates.
A reported Classical use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or persons, with the form used in a plural sense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a reported Classical usage associated with the noun's plural interpretation.
This synonymic use is reported with uncertain transmission and may reflect the related sense of neighborhood or protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating or attributable to إِلّ, whether understood as God or as revelation or inspiration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression أَمْرٌ إِلَّىٌّ; the intended referent depends on the sense assigned to إِلّ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Modes of marking a noun as known.
Allusive use with transferred proper names.
Redundancy, inseparability, and poetic attachment rules.
Disputed syntactic analysis as an affixed-pronoun substitute.
Syntactic idiom and grammatical analysis without an independent lexical branch.
Reported neighbor synonym with transmission caveat.
Attributive derivative in the supplied expression.

cautions: The two Quran occurrences of إِلّ admit several reported readings: kinship, covenant or security, lordship, and God. The divine reading is explicitly disputed in the lexical evidence.
The Lane material also contains the separate function word ال; it is retained under other_classical_meanings and is not treated as a sense of the Quranic noun إِلّ.
